headline: Sellers in Control as Thursday Opens Under a Cloud of Inflation Data and Geopolitical Noise
body_html:
Futures point to a cautious open on Thursday after Wednesday's session left unmistakable damage across the board: only 124 names in our 545-stock universe closed higher while 417 declined, a lopsided ratio that underscores how broadly the selling pressure spread. The Consumer and Industrials sectors bore the sharpest losses, off 1.65% and 1.44% respectively, while Semiconductors — the lone bright spot — eked out a 0.54% gain as MaxLinear surged 7.5% and provided a rare counterweight to the gloom.

The single most important catalyst on today's calendar is the release of wholesale inflation data. Treasury yields were already moving higher ahead of that print, signaling that bond markets are braced for a number that could complicate the Federal Reserve's calculus. Any upside surprise would likely add fresh pressure to rate-sensitive corners of the market, including Homebuilders, already down 0.53% Wednesday, and Software, which shed 0.93%.

Geopolitical risk deserves a place on every watch-list this morning. Houthi forces are reportedly advancing toward the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a chokepoint through which a significant share of global energy trade flows. Energy was effectively flat on Wednesday at +0.02%, but a credible supply-disruption headline could reprice crude — and therefore energy equities — quickly. Watch the open with that tail risk in mind.

briefs.headline: Wholesale Inflation Print Is the Morning's Pivotal Number
briefs.body: Producer-price data hits before the open and arrives at a delicate moment: yields have already ticked higher in anticipation. A hotter-than-expected reading would reinforce the case for a higher-for-longer rate posture and could amplify the selling that dominated Wednesday's session across rate-sensitive sectors.

briefs.headline: Houthi Advance Toward Key Shipping Strait Raises Supply-Chain Alarm
briefs.body: Houthi fighters are said to be closing in on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, one of the world's most strategically critical maritime passages. The development threatens to reignite shipping-disruption fears; energy markets will be on close watch at the open after the sector barely registered a move on Wednesday.

briefs.headline: Macy's Raises Outlook as Turnaround Gains Credibility
briefs.body: The department-store chain reported stronger-than-expected quarterly results and lifted its full-year guidance, offering a rare upbeat signal from the beleaguered brick-and-mortar retail space. The news arrives as the broader Consumer sector was Wednesday's worst-performing group, down 1.65%, making Macy's showing all the more notable.

briefs.headline: VIX Hedging Picks Up Ahead of Historically Volatile Calendar Window
briefs.body: The so-called fear gauge is drawing fresh hedging interest as markets enter a stretch of September long associated with elevated volatility. Wednesday's heavily negative breadth — 417 decliners against just 124 advancers — lends credibility to the concern, and options desks may see heightened activity at Thursday's open.

briefs.headline: Algeria Severs Ties With UAE, Adding to Middle East Uncertainty
briefs.body: Algeria has cut diplomatic relations with the United Arab Emirates, according to Reuters, injecting another layer of regional instability into a market already monitoring Iran-related tensions and the Houthi push toward a vital Red Sea chokepoint. The move could weigh on sentiment in globally exposed sectors when trading resumes.

briefs.headline: NFL Eyes Australia Expansion in Ambitious International Push
briefs.body: League commissioner Roger Goodell is advancing plans for American football's debut in Australia, part of a broader international growth strategy. While the development is primarily a sports-business story, it has implications for broadcast-rights holders and event-infrastructure operators watching the league's expanding global footprint.
